neighbours.label: the first word of a parenthetical or self-interrupting aside (after '(' or ', or,' or a name followed by an exclamation: '(there is…', 'or, what I thought…', 'Blotts, what an awful name'): the pole marks the switch into an aside; the same words opening a plain sentence stay low
fire: The second album (there were only two) sold poorly at first.
He came from Leeds; or, what everyone assumed was Leeds.
Our new neighbor (it turns out) used to sing in an opera chorus.
Gertrude, what a lovely old-fashioned name, I said to her.
The recipe calls for saffron (there is really no substitute) and rice.
The meeting is on Thursday, or is it Wednesday, at the library.
These old maps (there are about forty of them) were found in an attic.
She called it a disaster; or, what she later called a lesson.
quiet: There were only two albums, and the second one sold poorly at first.
Everyone assumed that he came from Leeds.
It turns out our new neighbor used to sing in an opera chorus.
Her name was Gertrude, and I said hello to her.
The recipe calls for saffron and rice and a little butter.
The meeting is on Thursday at the library.
There are about forty old maps, and they were found in an attic.
She called it a disaster, and later she called it a lesson.
